request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This video follows up on an earlier one about the new Microsoft Copilot chat built into Business Central and walks through example scenarios in a demo. The presenter asks Copilot about sales tax setup for Oregon and California, and Copilot answers from outside sources and suggests follow-up questions. Next, Copilot analyzes sales data to find the slowest-selling items and suggests actions. The last scenarios use the presenter's calendar to find a customer meeting, prepare a sales brief from Business Central data, and give directions to the meeting. No release status, preview label or limitation is stated in the video.

chapters.title: Sales tax questions answered from outside sources
Calendar lookup and customer meeting brief

features.name: Microsoft Copilot chat in Business Central
features.description: A Copilot chat built directly into the new version of Business Central, opened from within the client. The video uses it for several question-and-answer scenarios.
prerequisites: The new version of Business Central

features.name: General questions answered from the internet
features.description: Copilot answers a sales tax setup question for Oregon by pulling data from the internet and other sources, then handles a follow-up about California. This does not use Business Central data.
caveats: This example did not use Business Central data

features.name: Follow-up conversation and suggested next steps
features.description: The user can keep asking questions in the same conversation, and Copilot offers suggestions for how the conversation might continue, for example determining correct ZIP codes for California.

features.name: Sales data analysis with Copilot
features.description: Copilot reasons over Business Central sales data to find items that sold the least in the last 3 months, links to those items and suggests actions such as bundling, promoting color variants and cross-selling.
caveats: Reasoning over data can take a little longer

features.name: Calendar access to find customer meetings
features.description: Copilot accesses the user's calendar and finds a meeting with a customer, including who it is with and where it takes place.

features.name: Customer meeting sales brief
features.description: Copilot pulls Business Central data related to the customer and prepares a sales brief with sales figures, sales momentum, account risk and recommended talking points.
prerequisites: Calendar access for the meeting lookup

features.name: Directions and questions outside Business Central
features.description: Copilot answers travel questions such as directions to the meeting location and public transport options. The presenter notes this is far outside the Business Central area and leaves the user to try it.
